STEP 1 - Scene: This is a small snack or side of two halved pieces of cooked yellow corn (corn cobs cut into rounds). Photographed from directly above on a white plate, with a few crumbs nearby.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a large square white plate, roughly 26 cm across (dinner-plate size). Area ≈ 3.14 x (13)^2 ≈ 530 cm² (treating the square plate as roughly this area).

STEP 3 - Items: Two cut corn rounds (sweet corn, cooked), plus a few tiny crumbs of kernel debris.

STEP 4 - Area: Each corn round is about 5 cm in diameter (roughly 1 cm of the plate per ~5 cm of corn), so each covers about 20 cm². Two rounds ≈ 40 cm², about 7.5% of the plate. Crumbs are negligible.

STEP 5 - Volume: Each round is about 5 cm diameter by ~2.5 cm thick (cob slice with kernels). Volume per piece ≈ 3.14 x 2.5² x 2.5 ≈ 49 ml; two pieces ≈ 98 ml. Note the cob core is hollow-ish, but the outer envelope is used per the method.

STEP 6 - Grams: Corn cut pieces with cob, bulk density ~0.6 g/ml → about 59 g. Cob is inedible, so I reduce the edible portion: the kernel fraction of a cob slice is roughly 60%, giving ~35 g of edible corn.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked sweet corn ≈ 96 kcal/100 g (boiled corn kernels around 90–100 kcal/100 g). 35 g × 0.96 ≈ 34 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Two small corn rounds on a large plate, roughly 35–60 g total and about 35–55 kcal, is plausible. I report the edible-portion estimate of 40 g (cob included as the plated weight is ambiguous) at about 90 kcal/100 g.

Result: about 40 g of cooked corn, roughly 36 kcal.
